title: 1997 AHSME Problem 27
statement: Consider those functions \(f\) that satisfy \(f(x+4)+f(x-4)=f(x)\) for all real \(x.\) Any such function is periodic, and there is a least common positive period \(p\) for all of them. Find \(p.\)

solutions.text: For \(u_n=f(x+4n),\) the equation is \(u_{n+1}=u_n-u_{n-1}.\) Starting from \(u_0,u_1,\) the sequence is \[ \begin{gathered} u_0,u_1,u_1-u_0,-u_0,\\ -u_1,u_0-u_1,u_0,u_1,\ldots, \end{gathered} \] so every such function has period \(6\cdot4=24.\) This is least because \(f(x)=\sin(\frac{\pi x}{12})\) satisfies the equation and has fundamental period \(24.\) Hence D is correct.
hints: Use \(u_{n+1}+u_{n-1}=u_n\) repeatedly to find when every initial pair returns
